paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 26 to 35 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 26 至 35 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: In what’s probably the craziest headline I’ve ever written, I’ve reported that 26 in livestock protection are happening with scientists painting eyes on the butts of cows. The experiment is based upon the idea that farmers who’re protecting their herd from lions would shoot and kill lions in an effort to protect their livestock. While this makes a lot of sense, it results in many lion deaths that 27 would have been unnecessary. Researchers in Australia have been 28 and testing a method of trickery to make lions think they are being watched by the painted eyes on cow butts.

This idea is based on the principle that lions and other 29 are far less likely to attack when they feel they are being watched. As conservation areas become smaller, lions are increasingly coming into contact with human populations, which are expanding to the 30 of these protected areas.

Efforts like painting eyes on cow butts may seem crazy at first, but they could make actual headway in the fight for conservation. “If the method works, it could provide farmers in Botswana—and 31 —with a low-cost, sustainable tool to protect their livestock, and a way to keep lions safe from being killed.”

Lions are 32 ambush（埋伏）hunters, so when they feel their prey has 33 them, they usually give up on the hunt. Researchers are 34 testing their idea on a select herd of cattle. They have painted half of the cows with eyes and left the other half as normal. Through satellite tracking of both the herd and the lions in the area, they will be able to 35 if their psychological trickery will work to help keep farmers from shooting lions.

paragraphs.sourceText: Resilience Is About How You Recharge, Not How You Endure
paragraphs.translationZh: 韧性是关于你如何充电，而不是你如何忍受

paragraphs.sourceText: A. As constant travelers and parents of a 2-year-old, we sometimes fantasize about how much work we can do when one of us gets on a plane, undistracted by phones, friends, or movies. We race to get all our ground work done: packing, going through security, doing a last-minute work call, calling each other, then boarding the plane. Then, when we try to have that amazing work session in flight, we get nothing done. Even worse, after refreshing our email or reading the same studies over and over, we are too exhausted when we land to soldier on with（继续处理）the emails that have inevitably still piled up.
paragraphs.translationZh: 答：作为经常旅行的人和 2 岁孩子的父母，我们有时会幻想，当我们中的一个人登上飞机，不受电话、朋友或电影干扰时，我们可以做多少工作。我们争先恐后地完成所有的地面工作：收拾行李、通过安检、在最后一刻打工作电话、互相​​打电话，然后登机。然后，当我们试图在飞行中进行令人惊叹的工作会议时，我们什么也没完成。更糟糕的是，在一遍又一遍地刷新我们的电子邮件或阅读相同的研究之后，当我们着陆时，我们已经筋疲力尽，无法继续处理不可避免地堆积起来的电子邮件。

paragraphs.sourceText: B. Why should flying deplete us? We’re just sitting there doing nothing. Why can’t we be tougher, more resilient（有 复原力的）and determined in our work so we can accomplish all of the goals we set for ourselves? Based on our current research, we have come to realize that the problem is not our hectic schedule or the plane travel itself; the problem comes from a misconception of what it means to be resilient, and the resulting impact of overworking.
paragraphs.translationZh: B. 为什么飞行会消耗我们的能量？我们只是坐在那里什么都不做。为什么我们不能在工作中更加坚强、更加坚韧、更加坚定，这样我们才能实现为自己设定的所有目标？根据我们目前的研究，我们逐渐意识到问题不在于我们繁忙的日程或飞机旅行本身；而在于我们的日程安排或飞机旅行本身。问题源于对弹性的含义以及过度工作所产生的影响的误解。

paragraphs.sourceText: C. We often take a militaristic, “tough” approach to resilience and determination like a Marine pulling himself through the mud, a boxer going one more round, or a football player picking himself up off the ground for one more play. We believe that the longer we tough it out, the tougher we are, and therefore the more successful we will be. However, this entire conception is scientifically inaccurate.
paragraphs.translationZh: C. 我们经常采取一种军国主义的、“强硬”的方式来保持韧性和决心，就像一名海军陆战队员在泥泞中奋力挣扎，一名拳击手再打一轮，或者一名足球运动员从地上爬起来再踢一场比赛。我们相信，坚持的时间越长，我们就越坚强，因此我们就会越成功。然而，这整个概念在科学上是不准确的。

paragraphs.sourceText: D. The very lack of a recovery period is dramatically holding back our collective ability to be resilient and successful. Research has found that there is a direct correlation between lack of recovery and increased incidence of health and safety problems. And lack of recovery—whether by disrupting sleep with thoughts of work or having continuous cognitive arousal by watching our phones—is costing our companies $62 billion a year in lost productivity.
paragraphs.translationZh: D. 缺乏恢复期极大地阻碍了我们恢复活力和取得成功的集体能力。研究发现，恢复不足与健康和安全问题发生率增加之间存在直接关联。缺乏恢复——无论是因为工作的想法扰乱睡眠，还是因为看手机而持续认知唤醒——每年给我们的公司造成 620 亿美元的生产力损失。

paragraphs.sourceText: E. And just because work stops, it doesn’t mean we are recovering. We “stop” work sometimes at 5 pm, but then we spend the night wrestling with solutions to work problems, talking about our work over dinner, and falling asleep thinking about how much work we’ll do tomorrow. In a study just released, researchers from Norway found that 7.8% of Norwegians have become workaholics（工作狂）. The scientists cite a definition of “workaholism” as “being overly concerned about work, driven by an uncontrollable work motivation, and investing so much time and effort in work that it impairs other important life areas.”
paragraphs.translationZh: E. 工作停止并不意味着我们正在康复。有时我们会在下午 5 点“停止”工作，但随后我们会整夜思考工作问题的解决方案，在晚餐时谈论我们的工作，然后在入睡时思考明天要完成多少工作。在刚刚发布的一项研究中，挪威研究人员发现，7.8%的挪威人已经成为工作狂。科学家们对“工作狂”的定义是“在无法控制的工作动机的驱使下过度关注工作，并在工作上投入过多的时间和精力，以致损害了其他重要的生活领域。”

paragraphs.sourceText: F. We believe that the number of people who fit that definition includes the majority of American workers, which prompted us to begin a study of workaholism in the U.S.. Our study will use a large corporate dataset from a major medical company to examine how technology extends our working hours and thus interferes with necessary cognitive recovery, resulting in huge health care costs and turnover costs for employers.
paragraphs.translationZh: F. 我们认为符合这个定义的人数包括大多数美国工人，这促使我们开始对美国的工作狂进行研究。我们的研究将使用一家大型医疗公司的大型企业数据集来检验技术如何延长我们的工作时间，从而干扰必要的认知恢复，从而给雇主带来巨大的医疗保健成本和人员流动成本。

paragraphs.sourceText: G. The misconception of resilience is often bred from an early age. Parents trying to teach their children resilience might celebrate a high school student staying up until 3 am to finish a science fair project. What a distortion of resilience! A resilient child is a well-rested one. When an exhausted student goes to school, he risks hurting everyone on the road with his impaired driving; he doesn’t have the cognitive resources to do well on his English test; he has lower self-control with his friends; and at home, he is moody with his parents. Overwork and exhaustion are the opposite of resilience and the bad habits we acquire when we’re young only magnify when we hit the workforce.
paragraphs.translationZh: G. 对复原力的误解往往是从小就养成的。试图教导孩子适应力的父母可能会庆祝高中生熬夜到凌晨 3 点完成科学展览项目。韧性是多么扭曲啊！一个有弹性的孩子是一个休息良好的孩子。当一个筋疲力尽的学生去上学时，他可能会因为不清醒的驾驶而伤害路上的每个人；他没有足够的认知资源在英语考试中取得好成绩；他对朋友的自制力较差；而在家里，他则对父母喜怒无常。过度劳累和疲惫与韧性相反，我们年轻时养成的坏习惯只会在我们进入劳动力市场时放大。

paragraphs.sourceText: H. As Jim Loehr and Tony Schwartz have written, if you have too much time in the performance zone, you need more time in the recovery zone, otherwise you risk burnout. Gathering your resources to “try hard” requires burning energy in order to overcome your currently low arousal level. It also worsens exhaustion. Thus the more imbalanced we become due to overworking, the more value there is in activities that allow us to return to a state of balance. The value of a recovery period rises in proportion to the amount of work required of us.
paragraphs.translationZh: H. 正如吉姆·洛尔（Jim Loehr）和托尼·施瓦茨（Tony Schwartz）所写，如果你在表现区有太多时间，你就需要更多时间在恢复区，否则你就有倦怠的风险。收集资源“努力尝试”需要燃烧能量，以克服当前较低的唤醒水平。它还会加剧疲劳。因此，我们因过度工作而变得越不平衡，让我们恢复平衡状态的活动就越有价值。恢复期的价值与我们所需的工作量成正比。

paragraphs.sourceText: I. So how do we recover and build resilience? Most people assume that if you stop doing a task like answering emails or writing a paper, your brain will naturally recover, so that when you start again later in the day or the next morning, you’ll have your energy back. But surely everyone reading this has had times when you lie in bed for hours, unable to fall asleep because your brain is thinking about work. If you lie in bed for eight hours, you may have rested, but you can still feel exhausted the next day. That’s because rest and recovery are not the same thing.
paragraphs.translationZh: I. 那么我们如何恢复和增强韧性呢？大多数人认为，如果你停止做回复电子邮件或写论文等任务，你的大脑会自然恢复，这样当你在当天晚些时候或第二天早上重新开始时，你就会恢复精力。但肯定每个读到这篇文章的人都有过这样的经历：你躺在床上几个小时，无法入睡，因为你的大脑正在思考工作。如果你在床上躺了八个小时，你可能已经休息了，但第二天你仍然会感到疲惫。那是因为休息和恢复不是一回事。

paragraphs.sourceText: J. If you’re trying to build resilience at work, you need adequate internal and external recovery periods. As researchers Zijlstra, Cropley and Rydstedt write in their 2014 paper: “Internal recovery refers to the shorter periods of relaxation that take place within the frames of the work day or the work setting in the form of short scheduled or unscheduled breaks, by shifting attention or changing to other work tasks when the mental or physical resources required for the initial task are temporarily depleted or exhausted. External recovery refers to actions that take place outside of work—e.g. in the free time between the work days, and during weekends, holidays or vacations.” If after work you lie around on your bed and get irritated by political commentary on your phone or get stressed thinking about decisions about how to renovate your home, your brain has not received a break from high mental arousal states. Our brains need a rest as much as our bodies do.
paragraphs.translationZh: J. 如果你想在工作中建立韧性，你需要足够的内部和外部恢复期。正如研究人员 Zijlstra、Cropley 和 Rydstedt 在他们 2014 年的论文中所写：“内部恢复是指在工作日或工作环境中以短期计划或计划外休息的形式进行的较短的放松时间，当初始任务所需的精神或身体资源暂时耗尽或耗尽时，通过转移注意力或转向其他工作任务。外部恢复是指在工作之外进行的活动，例如在工作之间的空闲时间进行的活动。”工作日、周末、节假日或休假期间。”如果下班后你躺在床上，对手机上的政治评论感到恼火，或者在考虑如何翻修房屋的决定时感到压力很大，那么你的大脑还没有从高度的精神唤醒状态中得到休息。我们的大脑和我们的身体一样需要休息。

paragraphs.sourceText: K. If you really want to build resilience, you can start by strategically stopping. Give yourself the resources to be tough by creating internal and external recovery periods. Amy Blankson describes how to strategically stop during the day by using technology to control overworking. She suggests downloading the Instant or Moment apps to see how many times you turn on your phone each day. You can also use apps like Offtime or Unplugged to create tech free zones by strategically scheduling automatic airplane modes. The average person turns on their phone 150 times every day. If every distraction took only 1 minute, that would account for 2.5 hours a day.
paragraphs.translationZh: K. 如果你真的想增强韧性，你可以从策略性停止开始。通过创造内部和外部恢复期，为自己提供坚强的资源。艾米·布兰克森 (Amy Blankson) 介绍了如何通过使用技术来控制过度工作，从而有策略地停止白天的工作。她建议下载 Instant 或 Moment 应用程序来查看您每天打开手机的次数。您还可以使用 Offtime 或 Unplugged 等应用程序通过策略性地安排自动飞行模式来创建无技术区。一般人每天打开手机 150 次。如果每次分心只需要 1 分钟，那么一天就需要 2.5 个小时。

paragraphs.sourceText: L. In addition, you can take a cognitive break every 90 minutes to charge your batteries. Try to not have lunch at your desk, but instead spend time outside or with your friends—not talking about work. Take all of your paid time off, which not only gives you recovery periods, but raises your productivity and likelihood of promotion.
paragraphs.translationZh: L. 此外，您可以每 90 分钟进行一次认知休息，为自己充电。尽量不要在办公桌上吃午餐，而是在外面或与朋友一起度过时光，而不是谈论工作。休掉所有带薪休假，这不仅可以给你恢复期，还可以提高你的工作效率和晋升的可能性。

paragraphs.sourceText: M. As for us, we’ve started using our plane time as a work-free zone, and thus time to dip into the recovery phase. The results have been fantastic. We are usually tired already by the time we get on a plane, and the crowded space and unstable internet connection make work more challenging. Now, instead of swimming upstream, we relax, sleep, watch movies, or listen to music. And when we get off the plane, instead of being depleted, we feel recovered and ready to return to the performance zone.
paragraphs.translationZh: M. 至于我们，我们已经开始将飞机时间用作无工作区，从而有时间进入恢复阶段。结果非常好。当我们登上飞机时，我们通常已经很累了，拥挤的空间和不稳定的网络连接使工作更具挑战性。现在，我们不再向上游游泳，而是放松、睡觉、看电影或听音乐。当我们下了飞机时，我们并没有感到精疲力尽，而是感觉恢复了状态，准备好返回表演区。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. It has been found that inadequate recovery often leads to poor health and accidents.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 人们发现，恢复不充分往往会导致健康状况不佳和发生事故。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Mental relaxation is much needed, just as physical relaxation is.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 精神上的放松是非常需要的，就像身体上的放松一样。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. Adequate rest not only helps one recover, but also increases one’s work efficiency.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38、充分的休息不仅有助于恢复，还能提高工作效率。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. The author always has a hectic time before taking a flight.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 作者在乘飞机之前总是很忙碌。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. Recovery may not take place even if one seems to have stopped working.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 即使一个人看起来已经停止工作，康复也可能不会发生。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. It is advised that technology be used to prevent people from overworking.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 建议利用技术来防止人们过度工作。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. Contrary to popular belief, rest does not equal recovery.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 与普遍看法相反，休息并不等于康复。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. The author has come to see that his problem results from a misunderstanding of the meaning of resilience.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 提交人发现他的问题是由于对复原力含义的误解造成的。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. People’s distorted view about resilience may have developed from their upbringing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 人们对复原力的扭曲看法可能源于他们的成长经历。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. People tend to think the more determined they are, the greater their success will be.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 人们倾向于认为他们的决心越坚定，他们的成功就会越大。

For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C)and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有 2 段。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A)、B)、C) 和 D)。您应该决定最佳选择，并在答题卡 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Children with attention problems in early childhood were 40% less likely to graduate from high school, says a new study from Duke University.
paragraphs.translationZh: 杜克大学的一项新研究表明，幼儿时期存在注意力问题的儿童高中毕业的可能性降低 40%。

paragraphs.sourceText: The study included 386 kindergarteners from schools in the Fast Track Project, a multi-site clinical trial in the U.S. that in 1991 began tracking how children developed across their lives.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这项研究纳入了 Fast Track Project 学校的 386 名幼儿园儿童，这是一项在美国进行的多地点临床试验，于 1991 年开始追踪儿童一生的发展情况。

paragraphs.sourceText: With this study, researchers examined early academic attention and socio-emotional skills and how each contributed to academic success into young adulthood.
paragraphs.translationZh: 通过这项研究，研究人员研究了早期的学术注意力和社会情感技能，以及每一项如何对成年早期的学业成功做出贡献。

paragraphs.sourceText: They found that early attention skills were the most consistent predictor of academic success, and that likability by peers also had a modest effect on academic performance.
paragraphs.translationZh: 他们发现，早期的注意力技能是学业成功最一致的预测因素，而同龄人的喜爱程度对学业成绩也有一定的影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: By fifth grade, children with early attention difficulties had lower grades and reading achievement scores than their peers. As fifth-graders, children with early attention problems obtained average reading scores at least 3% lower than their contemporaries’ and grades at least 8% lower than those of their peers. This was after controlling for IQ, socio-economic status and academic skills at school entry.
paragraphs.translationZh: 到五年级时，早期注意力困难的孩子的成绩和阅读成绩均低于同龄人。五年级时，患有早期注意力问题的孩子的平均阅读成绩比同龄人低至少 3%，成绩比同龄人低至少 8%。这是在控制了入学时的智商、社会经济地位和学术技能之后的结果。

paragraphs.sourceText: Although these may not seem like large effects, the impact of early attention problems continued throughout the children’s academic careers. Lower reading achievement scores and grades in fifth grade contributed to reduced grades in middle school and thereby contributed to a 40% lower high school graduation rate.
paragraphs.translationZh: 尽管这些影响看起来似乎并不大，但早期注意力问题的影响在孩子们的整个学业生涯中持续存在。较低的阅读成绩和五年级成绩导致初中成绩下降，从而导致高中毕业率降低 40%。

paragraphs.sourceText: “The children we identified as having attention difficulties were not diagnosed with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder（注意力缺乏多动症）（ADHD）, although some may have had the disorder. Our findings suggest that even more modest attention dean of Duke’s Trinity College of Arts & Sciences, whose research has focused on ADHD and interventions to improve academic performance in children with attention difficulties.
paragraphs.translationZh: “我们发现有注意力缺陷的孩子并没有被诊断为注意力缺乏多动症（ADHD），尽管有些人可能患有这种疾病。我们的研究结果表明，杜克大学三一艺术与科学学院的院长更温和，他的研究重点是注意力缺陷多动症和提高注意力缺陷儿童学业成绩的干预措施。

paragraphs.sourceText: Social acceptance by peers in early childhood also predicted grades in fifth grade. Children not as liked by their first-grade peers had slightly lower grades in fifth grade, while those with higher social acceptance had higher grades.
paragraphs.translationZh: 幼儿时期同龄人的社会接受度也可以预测五年级的成绩。不被一年级同龄人喜欢的孩子在五年级时的成绩略低，而那些社会接受度较高的孩子则成绩较高。

paragraphs.sourceText: “This study shows the importance of so-called ‘non-cognitive’ or soft skills in contributing to children’s positive peer relationships, which, in turn, contribute to their academic success,” said Kenneth Dodge, director of the Duke Center for Child and Family Policy.
paragraphs.translationZh: 杜克大学儿童与家庭政策中心主任肯尼思·道奇说：“这项研究表明，所谓的‘非认知’或软技能对于促进儿童积极的同伴关系的重要性，而这反过来又有助于他们的学业成功。”

paragraphs.sourceText: The results highlight the need to develop effective early interventions to help those with attention problems stay on track academically and for educators to encourage positive peer relationships, the researchers said.
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究人员表示，研究结果强调需要制定有效的早期干预措施，帮助那些有注意力问题的人在学业上保持正轨，并让教育工作者鼓励积极的同伴关系。

paragraphs.sourceText: “We’re learning that student success requires a more comprehensive approach, one that incorporates not only academic skills but also social, self-regulatory and attention skills,” Dodge said. “If we neglect any of these areas, the child’s development lags. If we attend to these areas, a child’s success may reinforce itself with positive feedback loops.”
paragraphs.translationZh: “我们了解到，学生的成功需要一种更全面的方法，不仅包括学术技能，还包括社交、自我调节和注意力技能，”道奇说。 “如果我们忽视这些领域中的任何一个，孩子的发展就会滞后。如果我们关注这些领域，孩子的成功可能会通过积极的反馈循环得到加强。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 51 至 55 题基于以下段落

paragraphs.sourceText: On Jan.9,2007, Steve Jobs formally announced Apple’s “revolutionary mobile phone”—a device that combined the functionality of an iPod, phone and Internet communication into a single unit, navigated by touch.
paragraphs.translationZh: 2007 年 1 月 9 日，史蒂夫·乔布斯正式宣布推出苹果公司的“革命性手机”——这款设备将 iPod、电话和互联网通信的功能结合到一个单元中，通过触摸进行导航。

paragraphs.sourceText: It was a huge milestone in the development of smartphones, which are now owned by a majority of American adults and are increasingly common across the globe.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这是智能手机发展的一个巨大里程碑，智能手机现在为大多数美国成年人所拥有，并且在全球范围内越来越普遍。

paragraphs.sourceText: As smartphones have multiplied, so have questions about their impact on how we live and how we work. Often the advantages of convenient, mobile technology are both obvious and taken for granted, leaving more subtle topics for concerned discussion: Are smartphones disturbing children’s sleep? Is an inability to get away from work having a negative impact on health? And what are the implications for privacy?
paragraphs.translationZh: 随着智能手机的数量成倍增加，人们对它们对我们的生活和工作方式的影响也产生了疑问。通常，便捷的移动技术的优势既显而易见又被认为是理所当然的，从而留下了更微妙的话题值得关注：智能手机是否会干扰儿童的睡眠？无法离开工作会对健康产生负面影响吗？对隐私有什么影响？

paragraphs.sourceText: But today, on the 10th anniversary of the iPhone, let’s take a moment to consider a less obvious advantage: the potential for smartphone technology to revolutionize behavioral science. That’s because, for the first time in human history, a large proportion of the species is in continuous contact with technology that can record key features of an individual’s behavior and environment.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但今天，在 iPhone 诞生 10 周年之际，让我们花点时间考虑一下一个不太明显的优势：智能手机技术彻底改变行为科学的潜力。这是因为，人类历史上第一次，很大一部分物种持续接触可以记录个体行为和环境关键特征的技术。

paragraphs.sourceText: Researchers have already begun to use smartphones in social scientific research, either to query people regularly as they engage in their normal lives or to record activity using the device’s built-in sensors. These studies are confirming, challenging and extending what’s been found using more traditional approaches, in which people report how they behaved in real life or participate in relatively short and artificial laboratory-based tasks.
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究人员已经开始在社会科学研究中使用智能手机，要么在人们的正常生活中定期询问他们，要么使用设备的内置传感器记录活动。这些研究证实、挑战和扩展了使用更传统方法所发现的结果，在传统方法中，人们报告他们在现实生活中的行为或参与相对较短的人工实验室任务。

paragraphs.sourceText: Such studies are just first steps. As more data are collected and methods for analysis improve, researchers will be in a better position to identify how different experiences, behaviors and environments relate to each other and evolve over time, with the potential to improve people’s productivity and wellbeing in a variety of domains. Beyond revealing population-wide patterns, the right combination of data and analysis can also help individuals identify unique characteristics of their own behavior, including conditions that could indicate the need for some form of intervention—such as an unusual increase in behaviors that signal a period of depression.
paragraphs.translationZh: 此类研究只是第一步。随着更多数据的收集和分析方法的改进，研究人员将能够更好地确定不同的体验、行为和环境如何相互关联并随着时间的推移而演变，从而有可能提高人们在各个领域的生产力和福祉。除了揭示人群范围内的模式之外，数据和分析的正确结合还可以帮助个人识别自己行为的独特特征，包括可能表明需要某种形式干预的条件，例如表明抑郁期的行为异常增加。

paragraphs.sourceText: Smartphone-based data collection comes at an appropriate time in the evolution of psychological science. Today, the field is in transition, moving away from a focus on laboratory studies with undergraduate participants towards more complex, real-world situations studied with more diverse groups of people. Smartphones offer new tools for achieving these ambitions, providing rich data about everyday behaviors in a variety of contexts.
paragraphs.translationZh: 基于智能手机的数据收集恰逢心理科学发展的适当时期。如今，该领域正在转型，从专注于本科生参与者的实验室研究转向更复杂、更多样化的人群研究现实世界的情况。智能手机为实现这些目标提供了新工具，提供了有关各种环境下日常行为的丰富数据。

paragraphs.sourceText: So here’s another way in which smartphones might transform the way we live and work: by offering insights into human psychology and behavior and, thus, supporting smarter social science.
paragraphs.translationZh: 因此，智能手机可以通过另一种方式改变我们的生活和工作方式：提供对人类心理和行为的见解，从而支持更智能的社会科学。
